en.title: Minimum Unloading Docks with a Fixed Start Order
en.description:
Trucks must start unloading in input order, and a free dock immediately takes the next truck; trucks that start at the same time are assigned in input order. All trucks must finish within time T; find the minimum number of docks. Trucks cannot be reordered.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n T; the second line contains each truck's duration. 1≤n≤50000, 1≤T≤10^15, 1≤duration≤min(T,10^9). The source has a note about reading the upper bound of T; this site explicitly uses 10^15.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 1 and 2. In the first example two docks would need 9 minutes, which does not meet the limit of 8.
hints: Binary search the number of docks. To check d, keep each dock's available time in a min-heap, assign each truck to the earliest free dock, then check the latest finish time.
